title: eval-harness: add CI prompt-regression gating + caching and parallel runs
author: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Add CI-level prompt-set regression gating to the eval-harness pipeline, with result caching and parallel worker support to keep runtime within CI budgets. Motivation: teams have started seeing regressions caused by prompt changes and model rollouts. We want an automated, deterministic CI gate that fails PRs when a prompt-set quality metric (e.g., exact-match / BLEU / rubric pass rate) drops below a configurable threshold compared to a baseline. This PR:  - Adds a new GitHub Actions workflow (eval/prompt-regression.yml) that runs a lightweight eval-harness job on a targeted prompt-set matrix.  - Implements a small eval-harness runner change to support:    * threshold-based gating (fail/pass)    * result artifact caching (store baseline/last-passing result blobs in S3-like storage)    * parallel worker pool to run prompt subsets concurrently and merge results  - Exposes per-prompt-set config in eval-harness/config/prompt_gates.toml with defaults and overrides by path or label  - Updates test infra to include a mocked storage backend for CI and adds unit+integration tests for gate semantics  - Adds docs and a short migration note in docs/eval/ci-gates.md Checklist:  - [x] design doc reviewed by infra and SRE teams (linked)  - [x] unit tests added  - [x] integration tests using mocked storage  - [x] docs updated  - [x] Linear and release notes added Related: ENG-8421 (linear), INT-1042 (incident follow-up), SUP-77 (customer report). Motivation/Constraints: The gate must be deterministic and cheap enough for PRs (<= 15m typical wall time). To achieve this we run a curated subset of prompts and use caching to avoid re-running unchanged subsets. Caveats: initial iteration only supports text-generation style prompts and the gating metric is configurable but enforced as a single numeric threshold per prompt-set. Future work: extend to structured-output evals, per-commit baseline updates, and cross-model comparisons.

notes: This PR was driven by customer regressions flagged in SUP-77 and an internal incident (INT-1042). The gating config uses conservative defaults and can be relaxed per-folder via prompt_gates.toml. The action is opt-in via label `run-prompt-eval` or by changing paths under eval/sets/.
migration_steps: 1) Review eval-harness/config/prompt_gates.toml and set thresholds for your prompt-sets. 2) If you rely on CI gating, add the `run-prompt-eval` label to the repo or include the path `eval/sets/` in your PR. 3) For on-prem/private installs, configure cache backend (S3 or local) in ci/settings.yaml.
follow_up: Track ENG-8604 for structured-output gating and ENG-8740 for per-commit baseline updates. Monitor false-positive rate and CI runtime in the next two weeks.
estimated_ci_runtime: ~9-14m (depends on matrix size); parallel worker default = 4
